edges.description: Loss of LPA signalling through this axis yields the underdeveloped, tightly curled hair that defines the recessive forms.
The same signalling loss produces the hypotrichosis that accompanies woolly hair in the recessive forms.

The review's term for the phenotype this axis produces is underdeveloped hairs, of which the abnormally thin shaft is one aspect. The edge records that attribution; it is not a separate measurement of shaft diameter.
Reduced LPA-EGFR transactivation leaves hairs underdeveloped, which is the mechanism behind the short, slow-growing shafts.
A disrupted inner-root-sheath keratin filament network distorts the shape of the hair shaft it moulds, producing the tightly curled hair.

nodes.description: LIPH (lipase H) is a membrane-bound phospholipase A1 that hydrolyzes phosphatidic acid to produce 2-acyl lysophosphatidic acid (LPA). LPA is the physiological ligand for LPAR6 (P2RY5), a G-protein-coupled receptor expressed in the inner root sheath of the hair follicle. Loss-of-function variants in either LIPH or LPAR6 disrupt this autocrine/paracrine LPA-signaling axis that is required for normal hair-follicle differentiation, producing tightly curled woolly hair and hypotrichosis. Reduced LIPH-LPA-LPAR6 signaling decreases transactivation of downstream EGFR signaling, resulting in underdeveloped hairs.

nodes.description: The hair shafts are abnormally thin / fine.

The inner root sheath keratins heterodimerise in obligate type I / type II pairs to build the keratin intermediate filaments that shape the growing hair shaft. KRT74 and KRT71 are the type II partners and KRT25 the type I partner curated here. Heterozygous dominant KRT74 or KRT71 variants impair filament assembly in the inner root sheath, and biallelic KRT25 variants disrupt the same filaments from the type I side, in each case distorting hair-shaft formation and producing woolly hair with variable hypotrichosis. This is a separate mechanism from the LIPH-LPA-LPAR6 signalling node: the keratin subtypes are not LPA-axis disorders, which is why a single entry carries two independent pathophysiology chains.
